name: dry_air_screw_compressor_leakage
title: Dry air screw compressor with internal leakage
summary: Dry (oil-free) screw air compressor between 1 bar / 15 C suction and 3 bar discharge: three parameters identified at the 7000 rpm nominal point (swept volume, mechanical-loss torque, equivalent leakage-throat area) are imposed, and the model predicts the performance at another speed (2000 rpm default) with the leakage flow through a choked equivalent nozzle mixed back into the suction, isentropic internal compression and mechanical losses dissipated to the surroundings.

authors: Vincent Lemort (ULiège Thermodynamics Laboratory, original exercise)
origin.course: ULiège, Machines et systèmes thermiques, repetition 2, exercise 1 (second part)

verification.reference: EES stored solution of thermo_models TM-0039 (VL050926_2-1-2 questionsVL051023.EES, EES 7.403, partial: inputs and suction state) and full stored solution of TM-0032 (MSTh-SB-R2-Ex1-2.EES, EES 7.458, SB variant at the same 2000 rpm point)
verification.notes: 16/19 stored variables of TM-0039 agree; the 3 absolute enthalpies/entropies differ by a constant reference-state offset (EES air_ha vs CoolProp Air, +125.97 kJ/kg on h) while energy differences agree (h_ex_s - h_su within 0.03 %). Against the SB variant (Air fluid, parameters within 0.15 %, gamma solved 1.395 vs fixed 1.4): all 16 comparable derived results within 0.15 % (M_dot 0.08 %, epsilon_v 0.05 %, epsilon_s 0.07 %, W_dot 0.04 %, M_dot_leak 0.14 %). No unit conversion needed (SI-C-Pa-J).
